title: The stalk maps of Spec of a ring map are the induced maps of localizations
statement: Let $\psi:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\operatorname{Spec}\psi:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the induced morphism of schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Q\subset R'$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=\psi^{-1}(Q)$, the image of the point $Q$ under $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$. Let $\lambda_{\mathfrak q}:R=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}$ and $\lambda'_Q:R'=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R',\mathcal O)\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R',Q}$ be the germ maps of global sections [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; they are localizations at $R\setminus\mathfrak q$, resp. $R'\setminus Q$, giving $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}\cong R_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R',Q}\cong R'_Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (1). Let $(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^\sharp_Q:\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R',Q}$ be the stalk map [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then $(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^\sharp_Q\circ\lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\lambda'_Q\circ\psi$; equivalently, under the two identifications, $(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^\sharp_Q$ is the ring map $\psi_Q:R_{\mathfrak q}\to R'_Q$, $r/s\mapsto\psi(r)/\psi(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
